name: Anthropic Agent Skills
description: Anthropic's official skills repository — first-party packs that teach Claude Code and other agents house workflows: document handling, spreadsheet and slide authoring, PDF work and more.
notes: The repository tree holds 19 skills plus a template directory; the largest skills project by a wide margin and the reference implementation of the format.
`npx skills add anthropics/skills` was verified by running it — the skills CLI lists and installs this pack like any other source.
Individual skills carry their own licences, so check the subfolder rather than assuming the repository licence covers everything.

name: OpenAI Skills Catalog
description: OpenAI's curated Codex skills catalog — 39 maintained skills covering PDFs, GitHub CI repair, Playwright automation, deployment to Vercel, Cloudflare, Netlify and Render, Notion, Linear, Figma and security review. Superseded by openai/plugins, but still installable.
notes: Deprecated by OpenAI: the repository README now directs new work to openai/plugins. The 39 curated skills still install and the repository is not archived — it was last pushed 2026-09-08.
All 39 entries under skills/.curated/ were checked one by one on 2026-09-24 and every SKILL.md resolves, including figma-use, migrate-to-codex, hatch-pet, winui-app and playwright-interactive.
skills/.system/ holds five further skills that ship with Codex and install automatically: imagegen, openai-docs, plugin-creator, skill-creator and skill-installer.

Skills widely listed online as OpenAI's — a .docx editor, a spreadsheet skill, Sora video and a web-game skill — exist at no path in this catalogue. Image generation does exist, but as the imagegen system skill above rather than a curated one.

name: Superpowers
description: An agentic skills framework and software-development methodology — a structured approach to planning, implementing and reviewing work with an agent, published as installable skills.
notes: 15 skills read from the repository tree, and `npx skills add obra/superpowers` was verified by running it.

OpenAI ships this methodology as a plugin of its own inside openai/plugins — an unusual case of a community project being blessed upstream. One of the most-starred repositories on GitHub; treat the stars as the reason to look, not the reason to trust.

name: ClawHub
description: The skills and plugins registry for OpenClaw — 942 skills from verified publishers in the feed ClawHub publishes, sitting in front of a much larger open catalogue of community uploads.
notes: The 942 counted here are the entries in ClawHub's own feed at /v1/feeds/skills (edition of 2026-09-24), which covers skills from verified publishers. It is the figure the registry publishes.

The open catalogue behind that feed is far larger and is not counted here: walking the site's listing API passed 12,892 unique slugs without finishing, and that endpoint is disallowed by the site's own robots.txt — so the open catalogue has no permitted, enumerable source and gets no number.
Skills install with `openclaw skills install @owner/slug`, verified against OpenClaw's documentation.

A skill URL cannot be checked with a status code: every /skills/<slug> page answers HTTP 200, invented slugs included. Checking one by hand works through the API instead — /api/v1/skills/<slug> returns 404 when a slug does not exist, 409 AMBIGUOUS_SKILL_SLUG when several owners share it, which is why @owner/slug is the only unambiguous reference.
Size and usage are different numbers: the top packages sit in the 100k–480k download range and most listings show none at all.
Includes a large Chinese-language catalogue alongside English packages.

name: skills.sh
description: A web directory for agent skills with a CLI installer, built to make discovering and adding a skill a single command.
notes: Moved from degraded to active: the registry has a public search API at skills.sh/api/search?q= that returns skill ids with install counts, which is how every skills.sh entry in this file was verified. The site's own pages still return HTTP 200 for any path, so only the API can confirm a skill exists.
/api/v1/skills requires a Vercel OIDC token, so the search endpoint is the usable one.

The CLI that powers it is open source (vercel-labs/skills, 32,380 stars) and `npx skills add <source> --skill <name>` was verified by running it against seven sources, including packs outside Vercel's own.
Install counts are lopsided: vercel-labs/skills/find-skills showed 3,539,754 installs against roughly 7,000 for CrewAI's four skills and a few hundred for smaller packs.

name: SkillsMP
description: An agent-skills marketplace indexing Codex and Claude skills, with browsing by creator and occupation.
notes: Moved from degraded to active: its current URL scheme returns honest 404s. /creators/<owner>/<repo>/<skill> resolves for real skills and 404s for invented ones, in both cases tested.
The older /skills/<slug> URLs that circulate in aggregator posts are dead — they return a page titled 'Legacy skill URL not found'.
The site advertises 200,000+ skills. That is its own claim: there is no public API and the catalogue is not enumerable in a way we could count, so no skill_count is stated here.
Much of what it indexes mirrors public GitHub repositories, so the canonical copy usually lives on GitHub rather than here.

name: Exa Agent Skills
description: Official skills for the Exa API — teaching an agent to call Exa's search and contents endpoints with cURL or raw HTTP when it already has URLs to read.
notes: Five skills, counted from the repository tree; `npx skills add exa-labs/agent-skills` verified by running it. Exa's own API has a free allowance, so the skill and the service it drives are both usable at zero cost.

name: Neon Agent Skills
description: Official skills for operating Neon serverless Postgres from an agent — branch creation, connection handling and database workflow tasks.
notes: 17 SKILL.md files counted from the repository tree, though the skills CLI lists 8 of them — the rest sit in layouts it does not traverse.
Pairs with Neon's free tier, which is already catalogued — a useful combination because the free plan's branching model is the part agents get wrong without guidance.

name: Weaviate Agent Skills
description: Official skills covering vector search, semantic and hybrid retrieval, data import, RAG cookbook patterns, agentic RAG and multimodal PDF search.
notes: Only two skills, counted from the tree — the smallest vendor pack here. It teaches retrieval strategy rather than an API surface, and hybrid search and chunking decisions are where RAG systems actually fail.

name: Apify Agent Skills
description: Official Apify skills for web scraping, data extraction and browser automation through Apify's actor platform.
notes: Five skills, counted from the tree. Apify has a monthly free credit allowance that covers light scraping; for a purely free path with no account, pair it with Firecrawl's free tier or the Playwright skill instead.

name: Microsoft Agent Skills
description: Microsoft's skills, plugins and custom-agent definitions for building on Azure SDKs and Microsoft Foundry — generated per service and language, alongside MCP-builder, documentation and workspace tooling.
notes: The repository now lives at microsoft/skills; the older microsoft/agent-skills path redirects to it, which is the link most aggregator lists still carry.

Counted from the tree: 204 SKILL.md files, 191 under .github/plugins and 13 under .github/skills. The README separately advertises 175 skills, so the two figures do not agree and the tree is the one we can check.

Scope is Azure SDKs and Microsoft Foundry, not the Bot Framework or Cognitive Services as aggregator descriptions have it. Marked work in progress by Microsoft; `npx skills add microsoft/skills` verified by running it.

name: Intellectronica Agent Skills
description: A maintained personal collection of agent skills, best known for a Notion REST API skill that drives workspaces with curl and jq rather than a vendor SDK.
notes: 44 SKILL.md files counted from the tree; the skills CLI lists 22, so the difference is layout rather than content we could see.
Its notion-api skill is one of the most-installed skills anywhere in this category — 78,501 installs in the skills.sh registry, second only to Vercel's find-skills among the packs measured here.
Single-maintainer project. The curl-and-jq approach works with any agent that can run shell commands, but the Notion API it targets changes independently of the skill.

The lowercase path redirects to SKILL.md; the filename is case-sensitive, so use the URL exactly as written.

name: OpenAI Plugins
description: OpenAI's current home for Codex skills and plugins — 62 plugin packages holding 536 skills, from first-party tooling to integrations published by Adobe, Atlassian, Canva, Cloudflare, Datadog, Figma, GitHub, Linear, Notion, Sentry, Stripe, Supabase, Vercel and more.
notes: Successor to openai/skills. Read from the repository tree on 2026-09-24: 62 directories under plugins/, containing 536 SKILL.md files.

Heaviest packages: twilio-developer-kit (55 skills), vercel (54), zoom (53), life-science-research (50), public-equity-investing (23), shopify (20), build-web-data-visualization (18), data-analytics (18), ngs-analysis (18).
Layout is one directory per plugin with skills, commands, agents, hooks.json and an .mcp.json, not a flat skills/ tree — the generic skills CLI does not traverse it, so these install through Codex.
No repository-level licence; each plugin carries its own LICENSE.txt.

name: CrewAI Skills
description: Official CrewAI skills for building multi-agent systems — agent and task design, project scaffolding, and a docs-aware helper for framework questions.
notes: Four skills, all four independently present in the skills.sh registry with roughly 6,900–7,100 installs each. Small repository, but it teaches design decisions (role, goal, guardrails, task dependencies) rather than API calls.

name: Vercel Agent Skills
description: Vercel's official skills for React and Next.js work and for shipping to Vercel: React best practices, composition patterns, view transitions, React Native, deployment, optimising cost and performance, plus web design and writing guidelines.
notes: Nine skills, including react-best-practices, web-design-guidelines, vercel-optimize, deploy-to-vercel and vercel-cli-with-tokens.
The same lab builds the skills.sh registry and its CLI, so these are the reference example of a vendor pack that installs cleanly through `npx skills add`.

name: Browserbase Skills
description: Browserbase's official skills for reaching the web from an agent — search without a browser session, fetch a URL, drive a full browser, convert a browser flow into an API call, trace sessions, run adversarial UI tests and research a company.
notes: Eighteen skills read from the repository tree. The pack distinguishes cheap paths (search, fetch) from expensive ones (full browser sessions), which is the cost decision agents usually get wrong.

name: browse.sh
description: An open catalogue of browser-automation skills keyed by site: each entry names a domain, a skill and the method that reaches it, so an agent can ask what is already known about a site before writing a scraper from scratch.
notes: Published by the Browserbase team; the CLI is the npm package `browse` ("Unified Browserbase CLI for browser automation and cloud APIs"), which we confirmed exists under Browserbase maintainers.
No count is claimed here: the catalogue is not exposed by a public API and the page does not state a size, so unlike the other registries in this file there is nothing to verify against.
Entries read like `sam.gov · contract-opportunity-search · api` — a domain, the job and how to reach it.

name: Exa Contents
description: Calls the Exa Contents endpoint with cURL or raw HTTP when an agent already has URLs and needs page text, highlights, summaries, links, subpages or per-URL status without an SDK.
notes: One of five skills in the Exa pack. 673 installs in the skills.sh registry. Exa has a free allowance, so both the skill and the API it drives are usable at no cost.
